question: Should oversized or mixed iOS shares fail closed and require the user to remove unsupported items and start the share again, rather than allowing the supported subset to be sent?
rationale: Both behaviors are technically implementable, but changing an established partial-send path into a hard block is a user-facing compatibility and delivery-policy choice that source inspection cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve fail-closed sending
options.body: Land the blocking behavior after exact-head native proof confirms omitted content cannot be sent and ordinary supported shares remain unchanged.

options.title: Require explicit partial-send consent
options.body: Preserve a user-controlled partial-send option while clearly listing omitted attachments, which avoids an unconditional compatibility break but requires additional UX work.

options.title: Pause for broader transport support
options.body: Defer this patch until videos and files can be transported, leaving the silent-loss bug unresolved in the interim.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed sending
recommendation.body: Land the blocking behavior after exact-head native proof confirms omitted content cannot be sent and ordinary supported shares remain unchanged.
